name: Impossible Burger (Composite)
notes:
Impossible Burger modelled from its ingredients (a composite), rather than from its own LCA. The 'Impossible Meat' entry is the same product modelled from Impossible Foods' Quantis LCA instead.

The recipe is worked out from the 2023 label: ~22% soy protein concentrate, ~5.5% each sunflower and coconut oil (solved from total and saturated fat), ~5% minor ingredients, ~62% water. Soy protein concentrate is traced back to soybeans. Crop impacts (land, water, pesticides, farm emissions) come from those ingredients' own entries. Factory emissions (~2.3 kg CO2e/kg) come from the Quantis LCA, including heme fermentation, and are added on top.

Availability blends the product's own volume (~2.7 Gg/yr, from the 2018 Oakland plant) with its ingredients' world supply, so it isn't penalised for being a small brand. The recipe shares are confidence 2: labels only give ingredient order, not amounts.

source.title: USDA FoodData Central — Impossible Foods, Burger Patties Made From Plants (Branded, FDC 2664240, 2023)
source.note: Impossible Meat — nutrition: FDC 2664240 (Impossible Foods label, 2023 recipe) per 100 g raw: 204 kcal, fat 11.5 g, sat fat 5.31 g, protein 16.81 g, fiber 4.4 g, sodium 327 mg, carbs 7.96 g, sugars 0.88 g, cholesterol 0, trans fat 0; converted to per gram. Raw (as purchased) values.

source.title: USDA FoodData Central — Impossible Foods, Burger Patties Made From Plants (Branded, FDC 2664240, 2023)
source.note: Impossible Burger — soy protein concentrate (SPC) share: label protein 16.8 g/100 g, almost all from SPC at ~70% protein (dry) -> ~0.24 kg SPC/kg, less ~0.02 for the small soy protein isolate / yeast extract share -> 0.22. Label ingredient order (FDC 2664240, 2023 recipe): water, soy protein concentrate, sunflower oil, coconut oil, natural flavors, then <=2% each of methylcellulose, dextrose, starch, yeast extract, soy leghemoglobin, salt, vitamins.

source.title: Khan et al. / Quantis (2019) — Comparative Environmental LCA of the Impossible Burger with Conventional Ground Beef Burger (Final Report, 27 Feb 2019)
source.note: Impossible Burger — kg soybeans charged per kg SPC: ~1.7 kg beans make 1 kg SPC by mass (0.79 kg meal per kg beans x ~0.75 SPC yield from meal), but the beans also yield ~0.19 kg oil. With economic allocation (meal carries ~60% of the bean's impact, as in the soy entry's farm-gate note) that is ~0.76 kg bean-equivalent per kg meal / 0.75 -> ~1.0 per kg SPC. Cross-check: Quantis gives soy protein ~24% of 2.5 m2·yr/kg = 0.6 m2 per kg burger, i.e. ~0.2 kg beans at US yields, same as 0.22 x 1.0.

source.note: Impossible Burger — sunflower oil share: solved from label fat 11.5 g and sat fat 5.31 g per 100 g, assuming the two oils supply the fat, coconut oil ~86% saturated and sunflower oil ~10%: coconut 0.055, sunflower 0.055 kg/kg. Label ingredient order (FDC 2664240, 2023 recipe): water, soy protein concentrate, sunflower oil, coconut oil, natural flavors, then <=2% each of methylcellulose, dextrose, starch, yeast extract, soy leghemoglobin, salt, vitamins.

source.title: Khan et al. / Quantis (2019) — Comparative Environmental LCA of the Impossible Burger with Conventional Ground Beef Burger (Final Report, 27 Feb 2019)
source.note: Impossible Burger — processing emissions: Quantis Table 15 total 3.50 kg CO2e/kg = ingredients 2.09 + production 1.38 + packaging 0.02. Production + packaging = 1.40 (factory electricity, refrigerants). The ingredient stage also includes non-crop inputs, led by heme (LegH) fermentation; estimated as 2.09 minus crops modelled here (~0.85: soy, sunflower oil, coconut oil at this dataset's farm-gate values) minus potato protein (~9% of total = 0.32, dropped from the current recipe) = ~0.9. 1.40 + 0.9 = 2.3. Derived, confidence 2.

source.title: Khan et al. / Quantis (2019) — Comparative Environmental LCA of the Impossible Burger with Conventional Ground Beef Burger (Final Report, 27 Feb 2019)
source.note: Impossible Burger — processing water: Quantis Table 15 production 22.13 + packaging 0.19 L/kg, plus 8.5 L/kg for coconut oil refining (Sec. 5.2.1) = ~31 L/kg, counted as blue water. Heme fermentation water is not broken out in the report and is not included.

source.title: Fast Company (2018) — Impossible Foods is making 500,000 pounds of fake meat a month
source.note: Impossible Burger — availability_gg (product's own): 2018 Oakland plant ramp-up to 500,000 lb/month = 6 million lb/yr = 2,722 t = 2.7 Gg. Only public volume found; later output (co-manufacturers, more retail) is likely higher. Confidence 1. The pipeline blends this with the ingredients' world supply.

name: Beyond Burger (Composite)
notes:
Beyond Burger modelled from its ingredients (a composite). The recipe is worked out from the label: ~19% pea protein, ~7% canola oil, ~4% coconut oil, ~3% rice protein, ~7% minor ingredients (flavours, yeast, cocoa butter, methylcellulose), ~60% water. The oil shares are solved from total and saturated fat; rice protein is a rough estimate (confidence 1).

Crop impacts come from the ingredients' entries: pea protein traces back to peas, rice protein to rice. Factory, packaging, cold storage and ingredient transport emissions (~1.7 kg CO2e/kg) come from the Heller & Keoleian 2018 University of Michigan LCA.

Availability blends Beyond Meat's 2024 sales volume (31.8 Gg, all products, so it overstates the burger) with its ingredients' supply.

source.note: Beyond Burger — nutrition: FDC 2367272 (Beyond Meat label) per 100 g raw: 204 kcal, fat 12.4 g, sat fat 4.42 g, protein 17.7 g, fiber 1.8 g, sodium 345 mg, carbs 6.19 g, sugars 0, cholesterol 0, trans fat 0; converted to per gram. Same values as Beyond Beef ground (FDC 2663629, 2023).

Label (FDC 2367272): water, pea protein, expeller-pressed canola oil, refined coconut oil, rice protein, natural flavors, dried yeast, cocoa butter, methylcellulose, then <=1% each of potato starch, salt, potassium chloride, beet juice color, apple extract, pomegranate concentrate, sunflower lecithin, vinegar, lemon juice concentrate, vitamins.

source.title: Heller & Keoleian (2018) — Beyond Meat's Beyond Burger Life Cycle Assessment (Univ. of Michigan Center for Sustainable Systems, CSS18-10)
source.note: Beyond Burger — processing emissions: Heller & Keoleian 2018 Table 8 (per 0.113 kg patty, cradle to distribution, total 0.38 kg CO2e = 3.4 kg/kg): processing 0.05 + packaging 0.08 + cold storage 0.01 = 0.14; plus ingredient transport (6% of total, Table 9) 0.023; plus non-crop minor ingredients ~0.03 (ingredient stage 0.22 minus pea protein 20%, canola 12%, coconut 7% and transport 6% of total). Sum ~0.19 per patty = 1.7 kg/kg. Distribution to retail (0.02) excluded to match other composites. Recipe then was Beyond Burger 1.0, similar ingredients. Confidence 2.

name: Violife Just Like Parmesan (Composite)
notes:
Violife's vegan Parmesan-style wedge, modelled from its ingredients. The recipe comes from the US label: ~17.5% coconut oil, ~28% potato starch, ~6% rice starch, ~3% rice protein, ~3.5% salt, ~40% water. Coconut oil and potato starch are the main crop impacts.

The non-crop part (manufacturing, packaging, distribution, retail) is 2.1 kg CO2e/kg. That's Quantis' 2022 LCA total for this product (3.4) minus the crops modelled here.

Upfield publishes no Violife volumes, so its own availability is a deliberately low guess (0.5 Gg/yr, confidence 1), blended with its ingredients' supply. The nutrition is weak on protein (about 3.6 g per 100 g), which is the main reason it trails dairy Parmesan on nutrition.

source.note: Violife Parmesan — processing emissions: Quantis 2022 (source 413) gives 3.4 kg CO2e/kg for the US Parmesan-style wedge, cradle to grave (farming, manufacturing, packaging, distribution, retail, consumer use, packaging end-of-life; food waste excluded). name: Follow Your Heart Parmesan Grated (Composite)
notes:
Follow Your Heart's grated vegan Parmesan, modelled from its ingredients. The recipe is worked out from the label: ~40% modified potato starch, ~18% palm oil and ~12% canola oil (solved from total and saturated fat), ~5% each cellulose, maltodextrin and minor ingredients, ~15% water.

There's no LCA for this product, so factory and packaging emissions reuse the Violife Parmesan figure (2.1 kg CO2e/kg; confidence 1). Palm oil brings tropical-forest land into the land-use score.

Own availability is a deliberately low guess (0.2 Gg/yr), blended with its ingredients' supply. The label's 5 g serving makes the nutrition values coarse (confidence 3).

name: Coca-Cola (Composite)
notes:
Regular Coca-Cola, modelled from its ingredients: 10.6% sugar by weight (39 g per 355 mL can), split 85% cane / 15% beet like world sugar supply. The rest is carbonated water, caramel colour, phosphoric acid, flavours and caffeine, which have no crop footprint. The US version uses high fructose corn syrup, which isn't modelled.

Nutrition is from Coke's own label. It's pure sugar calories and has the worst nutrition score in the dataset.

Factory, can, distribution, chilling and disposal emissions (0.44 kg CO2e/kg) come from the Carbon Trust–certified footprint of a Diet Coke can (150 g CO2e, GB 2009). Diet Coke is the same drink without sugar, so this covers everything except the sugar crop. A glass bottle has more than double the footprint of a can. Factory water is Coca-Cola's reported 1.78 L per L of drink.

source.title: Coca-Cola US — Coca-Cola Original nutrition facts and ingredients
source.note: Coca-Cola — nutrition per gram: 140 kcal, 39 g sugar (= carbs), 45 mg sodium, 0 fat/protein per can ÷ 369 g. Label per 355 mL can × ~1.04 g/mL (a ~10.5% sugar solution) = 369 g per can. USDA generic regular cola (SR 14148, FDC 174852) is similar: 42 kcal, 9.94 g sugar, 3 mg sodium per 100 g.

source.title: Coca-Cola US — Coca-Cola Original nutrition facts and ingredients
source.note: Coca-Cola — cane sugar share: total sugar 39 g / 369 g = 0.1056 kg/kg, split by world sugar supply 85% cane / 15% beet (Wilmar 2024, ~152 of ~180 Mt). The US version uses high fructose corn syrup, which is not modelled.

source.title: Coca-Cola US — Coca-Cola Original nutrition facts and ingredients
source.note: Coca-Cola — beet sugar share: 15% of the 0.1056 kg sugar per kg (world supply split). British Coca-Cola is largely beet-sweetened.

ingredients.label: carbonated water, caramel color, phosphoric acid, natural flavors, caffeine

source.title: Coca-Cola US — Coca-Cola Original nutrition facts and ingredients
source.note: Coca-Cola — everything except sugar: carbonated water plus caramel color, phosphoric acid, flavors and caffeine (~34 mg per can). No crop footprint modelled; their emissions are inside processing_emissions_per_kg.

source.title: Talking Retail (2009) — Coca-Cola announces the carbon footprint of some of its top-sellers (Carbon Trust certified, Great Britain)
source.note: Coca-Cola — processing emissions: Diet Coke 330 mL can = 150 g CO2e full life cycle (Carbon Trust certified, GB 2009). Diet Coke is the same drink without sugar, so 150 g covers water, flavors, can, manufacture, distribution, retail, chilling and disposal but not the sugar crop. ÷ (330 mL × 1.04 g/mL = 343 g) = 0.44 kg CO2e/kg. Cross-check: regular Coca-Cola can 170 g, the 20 g difference ≈ 35 g sugar × ~0.6 kg CO2e/kg beet sugar. Cans; a glass bottle was 360 g (more than double).

source.title: The Coca-Cola Company (2025) — 2024 Environmental Update
source.note: Coca-Cola — processing water: Coca-Cola system water use ratio 1.78 L water per L of product (2023 and 2024) ÷ 1.04 kg/L = 1.71 L/kg. Includes the water that ends up in the drink. Added as blue water on top of the sugar crops' water.
